questions.background: Brendon McCullum currently coaches England's men's Test cricket team.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : An official England and Wales Cricket Board appointment announcement or reliable contemporaneous reporting of that announcement. Resolution : Resolve to the first person formally appointed as McCullum's permanent successor as head coach of England's men's Test team. Interim appointments and appointments solely concerning limited-overs cricket do not count. Resolution occurs when the appointment is announced, even if the coach begins work later. Accepted Answer Format : The appointed coach's full name.
questions.current_reasoning: Major 2026-07-17 update: frontrunner Andy Flower publicly and formally ruled himself out of the England Test head coach race at London Spirit's media day (BBC Sport, Sky Sports, Reuters, ESPNcricinfo, Hindustan Times), confirming he turned down the ECB even with dual-role IPL flexibility because IPL/RCB duties clash with the early English summer. Following Flower's withdrawal, iNews Cricket Correspondent Chris Stocks reports on July 17 that the ECB is now pivoting to former Australia coach Justin Langer as its top target (rated 4/5; strong Ashes rebuilding pedigree and county familiarity, though tempered by LSG IPL ties and past intensity concerns), lifting Langer 0.13 -> 0.26. Newly available Stephen Fleming (co-rated 4/5 by iNews, named by BBC Sport July 17) rises 0.19 -> 0.25 as he just left CSK after 18 years—removing the IPL clash that deterred Flower—was Rob Key's 2022 preference, and publicly welcomed an approach this week. Among remaining shortlisted contenders, Jonathan Trott (0.15 -> 0.16, English, available, named by BBC Sport/iNews 3/5), Richard Dawson (0.07 -> 0.09, English, ECB pathway, named by BBC Sport July 17), and Tom Moody (new entry at 0.07, explicitly named by BBC Sport July 17 alongside Trott, Dawson, and Fleming) round out the top 5, leaving 17% residual for Kumar Sangakkara, Mike Hesson, Adi Birrell, and unlisted options as BBC notes the ECB is still in an initial stage and open to an interim for August's Pakistan series.

questions.title: Which Federal Reserve policymakers will vote for an interest-rate increase at the July 29, 2026 FOMC meeting?
questions.background: The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) sets US monetary policy. Its policy announcements disclose members' votes and the policy preferences of dissenting voters.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : The Federal Reserve's official policy statement and voting record for the meeting concluding July 29, 2026, corroborated by contemporaneous news reporting. Resolution : Identify every voting member whose recorded position favors increasing the federal funds target range relative to the range immediately before the meeting. Include those members whether an increase is adopted or they dissent in favor of one. Accepted Answer Format : All qualifying members' surnames, listed alphabetically and separated by commas.
questions.current_reasoning: Major pre-blackout hawkish escalation on 2026-07-16 and 2026-07-17 (Reuters, CNBC, Khaleej Times) ahead of today's FOMC blackout start: AFTER seeing both cooler June CPI (-0.4% MoM) and PPI (-0.3% MoM), Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan delivered on July 16 what CNBC called 'the most specific call for a hike' among Fed voters ('I currently believe modestly higher interest rates would better balance the outlook... One month of relief is not enough... Better modest restriction now than severe restriction later'), and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack doubled down on LinkedIn on July 17 ('Inflation is too high... businesses say we need to take action... Persistently high inflation is the bigger concern'). Both dissented together in April, while Thursday retail sales prompted Q2 GDP upgrades and oil jumped >4% on July 17 on US-Iran escalation; CME FedWatch still prices ~88%-89% hold (~11%-12.3% hike), with NY Fed's Williams favoring hold, Vice Chair Jefferson conditional, and Chair Warsh noncommittal. This shifts substantial probability from solo 'Hammack' (0.22 -> 0.15) and unanimous hold into the twin dissent 'Hammack, Logan' (0.18 -> 0.28, new #1), solo 'Logan' (0.05 -> 0.10), and the April trio 'Hammack, Kashkari, Logan' (0.06 -> 0.10), while replacing 'Hammack, Kashkari' (unlikely without Logan after July 16) with 'Hammack, Logan, Waller' (0.03, as Reuters noted Waller demanded 'several months' of cooler readings), leaving 34% residual for a unanimous 12-0 hold, majority-hike coalitions, and other dissent sets.

questions.title: Which European country will announce plans to shut down its only nuclear power plant because of drought-related cooling-water shortages by August 2, 2026?
questions.background: Nuclear power plants that use river water for cooling can face operational restrictions when drought reduces the available water supply.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official government statements or contemporaneous reporting by established news organizations. Resolution Rule : Identify the European country whose government announces, between July 1 and August 2, 2026, inclusive, plans for a complete shutdown of its sole operating nuclear power plant because drought has reduced the river water available for reactor cooling. The announcement of the shutdown plan is sufficient; the shutdown itself need not have occurred. A partial reduction in electricity output alone does not qualify. Accepted Answer Format : The country's commonly used English name.
questions.current_reasoning: Important July 11 G4Media update from Nuclearelectrica corrects our July 9 assumption that Cernavoda Unit 1 remained offline: BOTH reactors at Romania's sole nuclear plant are operating at full nominal power and low Danube levels are not affecting operations for now—reducing Romania's immediate single-unit complete-shutdown vulnerability (0.30 -> 0.27). However, Nuclearelectrica confirmed Danube levels are low and explicitly cited tight complete-shutdown thresholds (2.50 mdMB for Unit 1, 2.35 mdMB for Unit 2—only 15 cm apart), keeping Romania a strong #2 alongside its August 2003 drought-shutdown precedent. Meanwhile, Reuters/Straits Times (July 12 & 17) reported temporary French reactor shutdowns (ineligible—multi-plant) and Western Europe's heatwave receding with rain, with no single-plant European country announcing a complete shutdown plan as of July 19. Slovenia's single-reactor Sava-cooled Krsko NPP edges up (0.34 -> 0.36), with Danube-cooled Hungary (Paks, 0.19 -> 0.20) and Bulgaria (Kozloduy, 0.13 -> 0.14) nudging up slightly and Belarus at 0.02 (sum 0.99).
